author: director
purpose: Acceptance suite for MP-5, the deterministic solver. Deliberately PROPERTY-BASED, not output goldens: a golden plan would break on every weight change and tell us nothing, whereas these hold regardless of which specific foods the solver picks. Requires no device and no Apple Intelligence.
howToUse: Generate plans for each profile in `profiles` at each horizon, then assert every applicable property. Report per-property PASS/FAIL with the violating day/meal/food. A property with severity `hard` failing is a blocking defect — it means the solver emitted a plan that is wrong, not merely suboptimal.
rules: Executors may ADD properties. Executors may NOT weaken or delete one to make a gate pass.
`hard` properties are invariants. There is no profile and no seed for which a violation is acceptable.
`soft` properties are quality objectives. Report the measured value; a miss is a tuning finding, not a failure.
An INFEASIBLE request must be reported as infeasible. Emitting a partial or silently-relaxed plan is a hard failure.

properties.assert: day count equals the requested horizon
properties.why: the most basic contract

properties.assert: each day has exactly the requested number of meals
no meal is empty
properties.why: an empty meal is an infeasibility being hidden

properties.assert: every component has grams > 0
properties.why: zero-gram components inflate variety without feeding anyone

properties.assert: every component resolves to a real FoodItem id present in the catalogue
properties.why: the solver must never emit an invented food

properties.assert: component count per meal is between 2 and 6
properties.why: one-item meals read as broken; seven read as noise

properties.assert: daily kcal is within ±18% of the profile target
properties.why: the band the reference solver holds across all profiles

properties.assert: day kcal equals the sum over components of FoodItem-derived kcal at that component's grams, within 1e-6
properties.why: MP-2's invariant. If this breaks, some path is inventing nutrition again.

properties.assert: day macro totals equal the sum over components of FoodItem-derived macros, within 1e-6
properties.why: same invariant, macros

properties.assert: daily protein is within ±25% of the profile protein target
daily fibre is at least 20 g for a 2000 kcal target, scaled proportionally
no component is a member of ANY excluded allergen concept, checked via FoodConcepts.members(of:) including hierarchy rollup and ingredient propagation
properties.why: THE critical property. Name matching is not sufficient — a recipe with a dairy ingredient must be caught even when its name has no dairy word.

properties.assert: no component is in the profile's excluded/disliked id set
no component is in AyurvedaRecommendationGate.excludedFoodIds
properties.why: the D9 never-recommend set: betel nut, vanaspati

properties.assert: no component's AUTHORED minAgeMonths floor exceeds the profile age, where authored means ageProvenance=authored per WE-8c
properties.why: legacyImport floors badge but do not hide — that ruling must hold in the solver too

properties.assert: no meal contains a hard viruddha pair
properties.why: severity 1.0 rules only: milk+fish, honey+ghee at equal parts, honey heated

properties.assert: soft viruddha pairs are counted and reported per plan
properties.why: exemptible per Ca.Su.26/104-106; report, do not block

properties.assert: no food id repeats within the no-repeat window (default 2 days)
for any meal slot across days, component sets differ by at least two components
properties.why: the rule the old prompt tried and failed to enforce in prose

properties.assert: a 7-day plan uses at least 25 distinct food ids
properties.why: guards against a solver that finds one good combination and repeats it

properties.assert: when a dosha imbalance is set, the plan's mean signed effect on THAT dosha is negative (pacifying) and lower than the same solver run with imbalance cleared
properties.why: THE test that the dravya data is actually driving selection. A solver that ignores dosha will show no difference between the two runs. This is the single most important soft property — it is the whole reason MP-5 exists.

properties.assert: for agni=slow, mean component heaviness is lower than for agni=balanced at the same kcal target
properties.why: manda agni tolerates less guru

properties.assert: for agni=slow, mean portion grams are lower than for agni=balanced at the same kcal target
properties.why: the portion multiplier is applied

properties.assert: rasa coverage across a 7-day plan reaches at least 5 of 6 tastes
properties.why: sarva-rasa-abhyasa (Ca.Su.25/40) is HABITUAL intake — measured over the window, never per plate. A per-meal six-taste assertion would be unsourced.

properties.assert: mean heaviness at the midday meal exceeds mean heaviness at the evening meal
properties.why: peak agni at midday; lightest at night

properties.assert: tier composition is reported: what share of selected components are classical, derived, estimated
properties.why: report only. If the solver selects overwhelmingly estimated-tier foods, the Ayurvedic scoring is running on the weakest data and the founder should know.

properties.assert: same profile + same seed + same catalogue produces a byte-identical plan, across two runs in one session and once after relaunch
properties.why: required for regenerate-this-day-only and for every gate here to mean anything

properties.assert: different seeds produce different plans for the same profile
properties.why: guards against a solver that ignores its seed and cannot offer alternatives

properties.assert: profile P10 is REPORTED infeasible; no partial plan is emitted and no constraint is silently relaxed
properties.why: the honest-failure contract. Quietly dropping an allergen to find a solution is the worst possible behaviour.

properties.assert: when infeasible, the report names WHICH constraint could not be satisfied
properties.why: so the UI can tell the user what to relax

properties.assert: a 7-day plan solves in under 2 seconds on the simulator
properties.why: the reference implementation does it in ~340 ms in unoptimised Python over 14k foods; Swift should be far faster. A miss here means an algorithmic problem, not a tuning one.

properties.assert: zero model calls during assembly, proven by MP-1 telemetry
properties.why: the entire point of MP-5

properties.assert: the solver completes with no FoundationModels linkage
properties.why: must work on iPhone 15/15 Plus and with Apple Intelligence off

properties.assert: no component is an infant or toddler product (infant formula, toddler formula, baby food, pediatric shake, follow-on formula) unless the profile age is under 36 months
properties.why: OBSERVED IN MP-6b: three separate infant/toddler formula selections in one week for an adult profile. minAgeMonths is a FLOOR, not a range — infant formula has a floor of 0 and therefore passes every adult age check. The data cannot express 'intended for infants, inappropriate for adults'; this property must.

properties.assert: every meal contains at least one component whose food role has `anchor: true` in food-roles.json (main or staple)
properties.why: OBSERVED: dinners composed entirely of spices, herbs and condiments. A meal needs something to be a meal.

properties.assert: per meal, at most 2 components total across roles `spice`, `herb`, `condiment` and `medicinalHerb`, and at most 1 `medicinalHerb`
properties.why: OBSERVED: 'Curry Leaves, Tulsi, Black Cumin, Lime leaf, Lentils raw, Nigella Seed' as a dinner; 'Garlic dried, Wild garlic dried, Garlic powder' in one lunch.

properties.assert: every component's portion grams fall inside the `portionGrams` min/max declared for its role in food-roles.json. The suite does NOT carry its own copy of these numbers — one source of truth.
properties.why: OBSERVED: exact 500/700/800 kcal totals were hit by scaling spices to implausible weights. Nobody eats 80 g of dried marjoram. Ranges live in food-roles.json so they cannot drift out of sync with the taxonomy.

properties.assert: no component carries the `notReadyToEat` flag defined in food-roles.json
properties.why: OBSERVED in four MP-6b meals as raw dry pulses. WIDENED in rev3 of this suite: the MP-7 G2c reverse census found 126 further rows that were eligible and not food you can put on a plate — unprepared frozen items, undiluted concentrates, commodity flours, refrigerated doughs. The flag now covers 301 rows rather than 100.

properties.assert: at most 2 components per meal have role `beverage`
properties.why: OBSERVED: 'Frozen yogurt chocolate, Chocolate milk, Milk shake with malt, Soy milk chocolate' as a breakfast.

properties.assert: no two components in the same meal satisfy `isNearDuplicateOf` as defined in food-roles.json
properties.why: OBSERVED: 'Marjoram, dried' beside 'Spices, marjoram, dried'; three garlic forms; two infant formulas.

properties.assert: report the role distribution across all selected components per plan
properties.why: report-only. If a plan is 60% spice by count, the objective is rewarding the wrong thing regardless of what the hard properties say.

properties.assert: no component has role `supplement`, `nonFood`, or `infantProduct`; that is, no component whose role declares `eligibleAsComponent: false`, except infantProduct for a profile under 36 months
properties.why: generalises C1 beyond infant products

properties.assert: report the count of catalogue rows resolving to role `other`, and the count of plan components with role `other`
properties.why: If the role map has holes, C2-C9 are enforcing a vocabulary that does not describe the catalogue. See the coverage gate in food-roles.json.

deletionNote: These exist to repair LLM output. A deterministic solver produces correct structure by construction, so they become dead code. Report any that CANNOT be deleted and why — that is a sign the solver is not covering something the old pipeline did.
revision: rev3 — 2026-07-27. C5 rebound to the widened `notReadyToEat` flag. rev2 — 2026-07-27. CRITICAL GAP FOUND IN MP-6b. The rev1 suite passed 23/23 hard properties on plans containing infant formula served to adults, breakfasts of four chocolate drinks, and dinners of six dried herbs beside raw lentils. No property asserted CULINARY PLAUSIBILITY. This revision adds group `plausibility` (C1-C10) and binds it to the new food-roles.json taxonomy. Director defect: I validated structure, nutrition, safety, variety, dosha, determinism, feasibility and performance, and never asked whether the output was food.
notes: FOOD ROLE is a new prerequisite. C2-C8 need every catalogue row to carry a role: main, staple, side, beverage, spice, herb, condiment, supplement, infantProduct, other. This does not exist yet and is a director artifact to author — it is the same shape as the FC-1 concept work and should live alongside it.

dependsOn.ayurveda-data/rules/food-roles.json: rev6 or later. Properties C1-C10 have NO meaning without it — it supplies the role vocabulary, the per-role portion ranges, the `notReadyToEat` flag and the near-duplicate test. Do not re-implement any of those inside the test harness.
dependsOn.ayurveda-data/tests/food-role-goldens.js: rev1 or later, plus the mandatory random holdout described in it.
